summary: Prod OOM resets on Dedicated GPUs correlated with long-context traffic (suspected KV cache fragmentation / allocation churn)
description:
Issue summary
- Customer reports repeated OOM-induced restarts on their Dedicated pool during bursty long-context traffic.
- Symptoms: GPU OOM -> runtime process exit -> in-flight requests fail; customer sees intermittent 5xx and elevated p99.
- Pattern observed: spikes coincide with increased proportion of requests using 24k–64k context and concurrent decode.

Customer impact
- Customer observed ~6–10 minute windows of elevated errors (HTTP 500/502) due to pod restarts and cold-start recovery.
- SLO risk: customer has internal requirement for low error rate during scheduled batch processing windows.

Customer-reported timestamps (UTC)
- 2025-02-17 23:40–23:55: first OOM burst
- 2025-02-18 01:10–01:20: second OOM burst
- 2025-02-18 03:05–03:12: third OOM burst

Environment details (from customer + our config)
- Deployment mode: Dedicated (single-tenant pool)
- Region/pool: us-east / ded-nbla-01
- GPU class: H100 80GB (8x)
- Runtime build: runtime-2025.02.16 (release train 2025w07)
- Scheduler policy: mixed prefill/decode, multi-queue by tier (customer is top tier within their pool)
- Max context (customer-configured): 64k
- Prefix cache: enabled (default)

What we saw internally (initial triage)
- Pod restarts in ded-nbla-01 align with GPU memory allocator failures.
- KV cache alloc failure rate increases before OOM events.
- Fragmentation ratio (where available) and allocator churn appear elevated during long-context bursts.

Evidence / logs
1) Runtime log excerpt (node: rte-ded-nbla-01-gpu-03, container: serving-runtime)
- 2025-02-18T01:11:42.913Z ERROR kv_cache_allocator: cudaErrorMemoryAllocation: out of memory
  request_id=rgw_01HS9ZQ6K6D3H9V2WZ0YJ9H3Q2 model=llama-3.1-70b-instruct
  prefill_tokens=64217 decode_tokens=0 batch_size=1
  free_bytes_reported=2147483648 largest_contig_bytes=268435456
  kv_cache_reserved_bytes=68719476736 kv_cache_in_use_bytes=62814515200
  note="alloc failed despite apparent free bytes; likely fragmentation / insufficient contiguous blocks"

- 2025-02-18T01:11:43.007Z FATAL runtime: GPU OOM during KV cache grow; aborting process

2) Scheduler stats around event
- Admission control started rejecting long-context requests only after allocator failures began (too late).
- Decode queue depth spiked; prefill queue drained unevenly.

3) Customer request distribution (from trace sample shared by customer)
- ~18% of requests at 48k–64k input context during burst window
- Many requests are single-turn long-doc summarization; little prefix reuse expected.

Suspected root cause (working hypothesis)
- Under long-context bursts with mixed sequence lengths, the KV cache becomes fragmented. Even with nominal free memory, allocator cannot find a sufficiently large contiguous allocation (or a compatible set of free blocks) and falls back to expensive paths, increasing churn.
- This matches known issue patterns in internal postmortems: allocator/eviction churn -> tail latency spikes; in this case escalates to OOM/restarts due to repeated allocation failures and retries.

Immediate mitigations attempted
- Increased admission control aggressiveness for >32k contexts during burst windows (temporary).
- Reduced max_context for this pool from 64k to 48k (customer-approved) while we investigate.
- Adjusted routing to avoid packing long-context requests onto already high KV cache utilization GPUs.

Escalation
- Escalated to Serving Runtime team for allocator/KV cache analysis and to propose longer-term fix.
- Requested runtime team to advise whether current allocator can safely apply stronger eviction or reserve strategy without destabilizing decode.

Customer comms
- Customer prefers we keep semantics unchanged (no model change), but is OK with max_context reduction if needed for stability.
- Customer requested an ETA for a durable fix; we cited the ongoing KV cache compaction workstream and committed to weekly updates.

Next steps
- Runtime: confirm fragmentation/allocator failure mechanism (Omar/Samir) and recommend safe per-pool knobs.
- SRE: add alerting on alloc failure rate + OOM restarts for Dedicated pools; ensure dashboards include long-context mix.
- Support: follow up with customer with mitigation summary and monitoring plan; gather a larger trace sample if needed.
comments: 2025-02-18 06:12 UTC - Rafael Mendes (SRE): Created ticket from overnight oncall notes. Correlates with pod restarts in ded-nbla-01. Paging Runtime for allocator failure analysis. Related Slack: #incidents thread 1739544202 (OOM + tail latency).

2025-02-18 07:03 UTC - Sean Gallagher (SRE): Confirmed 3 restarts on gpu-03/gpu-06 in 4 hours. OOM signature is consistent: kv_cache allocation fails -> process abort. Added temporary pool-level guardrail: cap concurrent long-context prefills to 2 per GPU (config change in scheduler).

2025-02-18 08:20 UTC - Omar El-Sayed (Runtime): Reviewing logs. The 'largest_contig_bytes' collapsing while 'free_bytes_reported' remains non-trivial is classic fragmentation symptom. Current allocator is not compaction-capable; eviction may not create the necessary contiguous space quickly enough under churn. Recommend (1) reduce max_context to 48k for stability; (2) bias admission control earlier based on predicted KV bytes; (3) temporarily disable prefix cache for the long-doc route (low reuse) to reduce metadata overhead/churn.

2025-02-18 09:05 UTC - Support (via Rafael): Sent customer mitigation proposal: reduce max context to 48k; enforce long-context concurrency cap; optionally split route for >32k with stricter admission control. Awaiting approval.

2025-02-18 10:14 UTC - Customer (Northbridge Legal AI): Approved reducing max context to 48k for now; asked whether we can restore 64k once stable. Also asked if this indicates a capacity shortfall. (We clarified this looks like allocator/fragmentation behavior, not raw capacity.)

2025-02-18 11:02 UTC - Sean Gallagher (SRE): Applied pool config: max_context=49152; enable early KV pressure gating; route label 'longdoc' to dedicated queue with lower parallelism. Monitoring for 24h. No further restarts since change (so far).

2025-02-19 13:37 UTC - Samir Qureshi (Runtime): Pulled allocator counters for ded-nbla-01. During pre-mitigation windows, allocation failure counter spiked 40–70/min and eviction attempts increased 3x. After lowering max_context, failures dropped to near-zero. This supports long-context trigger.

2025-02-20 16:10 UTC - Allison Grant (Observability): Adding recommended alert thresholds for Dedicated pools: (a) kv_alloc_fail_rate > 1/min for 5m; (b) oom_restart_count > 0 in 15m; (c) fragmentation_ratio > 0.35 sustained. Will align with upcoming KV cache health dashboard panels.

2025-02-24 18:22 UTC - Omar El-Sayed (Runtime): This is in-scope for KV cache compaction project. Linking PRs for instrumentation groundwork (pr-18423) and allocator refactor (pr-18431). Short-term: keep 48k cap until compaction flag can be safely canaried in Dedicated. We should also consider per-route policy: if input_tokens>32k then disable prefix caching and reserve larger KV blocks upfront.

2025-03-05 09:30 UTC - Rafael Mendes (SRE): Closing as Resolved (mitigated). 14 days without OOM restarts after changes. Follow-up tracked in runtime compaction project; customer will be notified ahead of any canary enabling in their pool.
resolution: Mitigated by reducing max_context from 64k -> 48k and enabling earlier KV pressure admission control + reduced long-context prefill concurrency in the Dedicated pool. No further OOM restarts observed for 14 days. Durable fix pending KV cache compaction rollout; ticket links added to compaction workstream for tracking.
